title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI
The patient is a 54-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports experiencing increased thirst and frequent urination over the last month. He states that his blood glucose readings have been consistently elevated. He currently manages his condition through diet and exercise alone. He denies any recent acute illnesses or changes in his daily activity levels.

Medication List
Diet and exercise only.

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. Physical examination reveals stable vital signs. Skin is intact without signs of infection. Neurological exam is unremarkable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hyperglycemia.

Plan
The patient will continue to focus on a diet-controlled regimen to manage blood glucose levels. We discussed the importance of consistent carbohydrate monitoring and regular physical activity. The patient was instructed to monitor his home glucose readings more frequently and return in four weeks for a follow-up evaluation.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
